derived_results.claim: If every proposal q_j and their convex mixture q_t retain q>=epsilon_min W, then H_t(j)=W_A^2Y/[q_t(A)q_j(A)] is bounded by 1/epsilon_min^2 while remaining conditionally unbiased for candidate second moment S_t(q_j). With epsilon_min=0.6, l_t(j)=H_t(j)/(25/9) lies exactly in [0,1].

For q_t=sum_j w_j q_j, S_t(q_t)<=sum_j w_j S_t(q_j) by convexity of 1/x. Thus a tracking-regret bound on weighted candidate second moments upper-bounds the actual mixture proposal's second moment and, after subtracting the proposal-independent target mean squared, its variance.

When the high-fidelity failure label Y=0, every proposal loss H_t(j) is exactly zero. Exponential loss updates may therefore be skipped. Fixed Share on the compressed sequence of nonzero failure events tracks expert switches in informative-event time; comparator switches inside zero-loss stretches can be moved to the next nonzero event without changing realized comparator loss.

An event-time Fixed-Share-style proposal mixture over epsilon={0.6,0.8,1.0} nearly matched r112 rolling hard selection while preserving a continuous defensive base component. On 150 held-out landscapes per start, cumulative variance was 182.8796 from epsilon=0.6 and 183.3903 from epsilon=0.8, respectively 4.98% and 2.85% below staying fixed and only 0.78% and 1.06% above a phasewise oracle grid.

engineering_update.scope: Engineering eta=16/share=0.01 per failure event is performance-tuned; formal numeric regret constants remain to be instantiated from a theorem-matched parameterization.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The current aggressive engineering eta is not theorem-optimal and carries no stated worst-case regret constant yet.
No-failure stretches contain no high-fidelity label information, so event-time adaptation cannot react before evidence arrives.
The favorable common bound 25/9 depends on the defensive epsilon_min=0.6 support floor.
Real agent trajectories and dependent resampling remain untested.
frontier: Instantiate a formal Fixed Share tracking-regret bound for the event-time bounded loss sequence and choose eta/share from an explicit switch budget.
Compare theorem-tuned and aggressive Fixed Share under abrupt, gradual and recurring drift using held-out common-random paths.
Derive an adaptive learning-rate/share schedule with an interpretable regret bound and near-engineering performance.
Extend the convex-mixture variance argument to dependent/systematic sibling resampling and random particle counts.
Build judge-guided proposal plus sparse high-fidelity labeling on an agent benchmark, preserving defensive base support and explicit likelihood correction.
exact_next_action: Write the event-time Fixed Share loss sequence as a standard bounded expert-advice problem, instantiate the Herbster-Warmuth tracking bound for J=3 and a chosen maximum number of switches, and map that bound through B=25/9 and S(q_mix)<=sum wS(q_j) into cumulative proposal variance units. Then validate theorem-tuned parameters against the eta=16 engineering setting on recurring drift. In parallel, prototype judge-guided proposal/high-fidelity correction on agent traces.
